for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i == j:
            dist[(i, j)] = 0.0          # self‑loops have zero cost (they will be forced to 0)
        else:
            dist[(i, j)] = dist_raw.get((i, j), BIG_M)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", nodes, lowBound=0, upBound=n, cat="Integer")

    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in offices if j != i) == 1, f"R1_depart_{i}"

# R2: each office must be arrived at exactly once
for j in offices:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in offices if i != j) == 1, f"R2_arrive_{j}"

# R3: tour starts (and ends) at office 1 → position of office 1 is 1
model += u[1] == 1, "R3_start"

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
supply = {
    "C1": 163,

    "C4": 62,
}

demand = {
    "W1": 157,
    "W2": 5,

    "W4": 217,
}

cost = {
    ("C1", "W1"): 8,
    ("C1", "W2"): 6,
    ("C1", "W3"): 14,
    ("C1", "W4"): 16,
    ("C2", "W1"): 16,
    ("C2", "W2"): 7,
    ("C2", "W3"): 13,
    ("C2", "W4"): 2,
    ("C3", "W1"): 6,
    ("C3", "W2"): 13,
    ("C3", "W3"): 1,
    ("C3", "W4"): 13,
    ("C4", "W1"): 9,
    ("C4", "W2"): 15,
    ("C4", "W3"): 10,
    ("C4", "W4"): 14,
}

centers = list(supply.keys())
warehouses = list(demand.keys())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Vehicle_Dispatch_Plan", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: integer, non‑negative
x = {}
for c in centers:
    for w in warehouses:
        var_name = f"x_{c}_{w}"
        x[(c, w)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Integer")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total fuel cost
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(c, w)] * x[(c, w)] for c in centers for w in warehouses), "Total_Fuel_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Requirements as named constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# R1 – supply limits (<=)
for c in centers:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(c, w)] for w in warehouses) <= supply[c],
        f"R1_supply_{c}"
    )

# R2 – demand satisfaction (==)
for w in warehouses:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(c, w)] for c in centers) == demand[w],
        f"R2_demand_{w}"
    )

# R3 – non‑negativity (>= 0) – explicit named constraints
for c in centers:
    for w in warehouses:
        model += (
            x[(c, w)] >= 0,
            f"R3_nonneg_{c}_{w}"
        )

# R4 – integrality is already enforced by variable type (Integer).
# If a named constraint is still desired, we can add a dummy equality:
for c in centers:
    for w in warehouses:
        model += (
            x[(c, w)] - x[(c, w)] == 0,
            f"R4_integrality_{c}_{w}"
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum total fuel cost:", pulp.value(model.objective))

for c in centers:
    for w in warehouses:
        qty = int(pulp.value(x[(c, w)]))
        print(f"  {c} -> {w}: {qty}")

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
alphas = ["Alpha1", "Alpha2", "Alpha3", "Alpha4", "Alpha5", "Alpha6"]
betas = ["Beta1", "Beta2", "Beta3", "Beta4", "Beta5", "Beta6"]

capacity = {
    "Alpha1": 110,
    "Alpha2": 123,
    "Alpha3": 108,
    "Alpha4": 73,
    "Alpha5": 161,
    "Alpha6": 75,
}

demand = {
    "Beta1": 244,
    "Beta2": 35,
    "Beta3": 58,
    "Beta4": 103,
    "Beta5": 10,
    "Beta6": 112,
}

cost = {
    ("Alpha1", "Beta1"): 2,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta2"): 10,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta3"): 12,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta4"): 12,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta5"): 14,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta6"): 5,
    ("Alpha2", "Beta1"): 8,

    ("Alpha3", "Beta2"): 3,
    ("Alpha3", "Beta3"): 20,
    ("Alpha3", "Beta4"): 13,
    ("Alpha3", "Beta5"): 20,
    ("Alpha3", "Beta6"): 8,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta1"): 16,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta2"): 19,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta3"): 5,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta4"): 8,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta5"): 15,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta6"): 9,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta1"): 15,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta2"): 9,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta3"): 1,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta4"): 15,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta5"): 10,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta6"): 18,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta1"): 6,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta2"): 3,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta3"): 15,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta4"): 12,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta5"): 19,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta6"): 10,
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Latency_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables (no built‑in lower bound, we will add explicit non‑negativity constraints)
x = {}
for i in alphas:
    for j in betas:
        var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
        x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=None, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total latency cost
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in alphas for j in betas), "Total_Latency_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Requirements as named constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# R1: capacity constraints for each Alpha cluster
for i in alphas:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in betas) <= capacity[i],
        f"R1_{i}_capacity",
    )

# R2: demand constraints for each Beta job
for j in betas:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in alphas) == demand[j],
        f"R2_{j}_demand",
    )

# R3: non‑negativity of all shipment variables
for i in alphas:
    for j in betas:
        model += (
            x[(i, j)] >= 0,
            f"R3_{i}_{j}_nonneg",
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Total latency cost:", pulp.value(model.objective))

print("\nOptimal shipment plan (units shipped from Alpha i to Beta j):")
for i in alphas:
    for j in betas:
        qty = x[(i, j)].varValue
        # Print only positive shipments for readability
        if qty is not None and qty > 1e-6:
            print(f"  {i} -> {j}: {qty:.2f}")

    [6, 11, 3, 8, 12, 8, 10, 14, 11, 12],   # F9
    [9, 19, 10, 15, 4, 16, 2, 19, 19, 20]   # F10
]

    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in range(num_f) for j in range(num_p)),
    lowBound=None,
    cat="Continuous"
)

model += pulp.lpSum(cost[i][j] * x[(i, j)] for i in range(num_f) for j in range(num_p)), "TotalCost"
